A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same P-CHECK work and contain complete, readable scientific sections and Appendix A. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendix material.

before.justification: v2 reports original reward-prediction and personalized-generation experiments, including Tables 1–4 and further empirical analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including benchmark results, ablations, robustness analyses, and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain identical checklist construction, contrastive sampling, saliency weighting, generator training, and reward-prediction procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use PRISM-Personalized, ChatbotArena-Personalized, and BESPOKE-MetaEval for the same tasks. Sparse-history, preference-shift, and other evaluation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment, including the reward-model baselines in Table 1, alignment comparators in Table 2, refinement baselines in Figure 5, and appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: The stated splits, model configurations, training settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures in Sections 4 and A.1 are identical. The added computational-resource acknowledgement does not revise any specified experimental setting.

E4.justification: The component ablations, sparse-history analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, cost analysis, preference-shift evaluation, checklist-quality assessment, and success/failure case studies are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same five-run reporting, 95% confidence intervals, and paired t-tests against the strongest baseline in Table 2. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including P-CHECK's 63.62% average accuracy in Table 1, generation results in Table 2, and appendix analyses and case studies.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–7 are identical. No definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims concerning dynamic checklists, preference-contrastive weighting, reward accuracy, personalized generation, and OOD robustness.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including difficulties expressing implicit preferences, propagation of checklist errors, training costs, and the appendix explanation of over-reliance on user priors.

D1.justification: The acknowledgement on page 10 newly credits computational resources from AWS Trainium via the Theta EdgeCloud platform. This adds resource provenance; the existing NVIDIA A6000 hardware descriptions, implementation settings, prompts, and code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are identical. Bibliography entries move across page boundaries without additions, removals, or substantive edits.

P1.justification: v3 extends the acknowledgement with computational-resource credit and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, section organization, and appendix text are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgement shifts the References heading and reflows bibliography text across pages 10–13. All figures and tables, including their captions and appendix placement, are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds computational-resource attribution but leaves the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility procedures, and limitations unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The acknowledgement and resulting bibliography reflow do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
